messages:
jessica: FYI customer AcmeCorp hitting 403 on /v1/chat/completions. They think they're using an org-scoped key. Posting the curl + response they sent. Can someone pick this up?

jessica: ```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-org_ABC123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

jessica: Response they pasted: `{"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"project not authorized","request_id":"req_z9x8y7"},"status":403}`

mike: can you get the exact request_id and timestamp from the customer? also need the raw response headers (x-request-id / x-rw-req-id if present).

jessica: they sent back `request_id=req_z9x8y7`, timestamp `2026-01-18T14:22:11Z`. Raw header they included: `x-rw-project: proj-52` and `authorization: Bearer sk-org_ABC123` (they redacted token after the prefix).

raj: hm that header looks like the client is passing a project header but using an org token. can you ask the customer if they copied the key from the project page by accident? quick repro idea: try the exact curl but with a project-scoped key to see if it flips to 200.

olivia: org tokens should start with `sk-org_` and be provisioned with org-scopes. project tokens often start with `sk-proj_` or `sk-project_` depending on UI. Also ask customer to run curl adding an `X-Request-Id` so we can trace server logs.

mike: I ran a quick local test: replaced Authorization with a project key I control (`sk-proj_TEST`) and re-ran the same payload + `-H \"X-Request-Id: repro-176945\"`. Result: 200, chat completion returned. With the org key from the curl above I reproduced the 403 and saw the same error body.

mike: snippet from my run: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` then body `{"error":{"type":"forbidden","message":"project not authorized","request_id":"req_z9x8y7"}}` when using the org key. With project key got `200` and tokens in response consistent.

jessica: I asked the customer to check which key they copied. they confirmed they grabbed the token under the project settings thinking it was org-level, then attempted to call the org endpoint. they said they have multiple dashboards open.

raj: action items: 1) ask customer to rotate the token and paste the prefix only so we can verify scope (we don't need entire secret) 2) ask them to call again with new org token and `X-Request-Id` to confirm 3) attach the server debug bundle if they still get 403 so eng can inspect (we need request_id+timestamp).

jessica: provided repro steps to customer + link to internal debug collector: https://internal.redwood/debug/collect?ref=1769456789 (customer-facing link redacted, support only). asked them to run:```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-key-prefix-goes-here>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: acme-176945" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}]}'
```

oncall-bot: Escalation created and routed to eng-oncall (#317). Ticket ID: ENG-5291 :white_flag:

olivia: small product note — we should make the error hint include `token-scope-mismatch` when header combo looks like project header + org-signed token. filing a tiny follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROD-1129

mike: marking as reproed locally. leaving steps + request ids in the ticket. jessica can you confirm with customer once they rotate keys? :thumbsup:
